# llm


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module connects the tutor to a model. The tutor needs only one
function, `ask(prompt, sp)`, which returns text. The module also parses
JSON replies and gives
[`Fake`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#fake), a model
for tests that runs offline.

Import the tools that this module uses.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### parse_json

``` python
def parse_json(
    s:str
):
```

*The first JSON object or array in `s`, also inside a
\`\``fence. Raise`ValueError\` when there is none.*

[`parse_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#parse_json)
reads JSON in a fence, JSON inside other text, and arrays. A fence
inside a JSON string does not break it. It fails when there is no JSON.

``` python
test_eq(parse_json('```json\n{"a": 1}\n```'), {'a': 1})
test_eq(parse_json('Here it is: {"a": [1, 2]} thanks'), {'a': [1, 2]})
test_eq(parse_json('[{"x": 1}]'), [{'x': 1}])
test_fail(lambda: parse_json('nothing'), contains='no JSON')
test_eq(parse_json('{"answer": "Use ```python\\nx = 1\\n``` here."}'), {'answer': 'Use ```python\nx = 1\n``` here.'})
test_eq(parse_json('Sure. {"a": 1} and then {"b": 2}'), {'a': 1})
```

## A model for tests

[`Fake`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#fake) replies
from a dict of rules. The first rule with a key in the prompt gives the
reply. It sends a dict or a list reply as JSON. It keeps each call in
`calls`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/llm.py#L70"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Fake

``` python
def Fake(
    rules:dict=None, dflt:str='{}'
):
```

*A stand-in model for tests:
`Fake({'grade': {...}, 'question': {...}})`.*

A matching rule gives its reply, and
[`Fake`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#fake) records
the call.

``` python
f = Fake({'GRADE': dict(correct=True)})
test_eq(ask_json(f, 'GRADE this'), dict(correct=True))
test_eq(len(f.calls), 1)
```

After a reply that is not JSON,
[`ask_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ask_json)
asks again and gets the JSON.

``` python
bad = Fake(dict(X=lambda p, sp: 'oops' if 'not valid' not in p else '{"ok": 1}'))
test_eq(ask_json(bad, 'X'), {'ok': 1})
```

With `need`, a reply must be one JSON object with text in each of those
keys. A list, or an object with no question, gets one more try. A second
bad reply raises a `ValueError` that names the key.

``` python
odd = Fake(dict(Q=lambda p, sp: '{"question": "What is a rank?"}' if 'must be one JSON object' in p else '[1, 2]'))
test_eq(ask_json(odd, 'Q', need=('question',)), {'question': 'What is a rank?'})
test_fail(lambda: ask_json(Fake(dflt={}), 'Q', need=('question',)), contains='question')
```

## A model for each task

The tutor does five tasks, and each task can use its own model. A quick
model can grade and give hints. A strong model can write questions and
lessons. The Settings page saves the choice.
[`Router`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#router) reads
it on each call, so a change has an effect on the next call.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>task</th>
<th>what the model does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>question</code></td>
<td>writes a question and its hidden model answer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>grade</code></td>
<td>reads the conversation and grades it</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>hint</code></td>
<td>gives the next hint</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>lesson</code></td>
<td>teaches the smallest step after a miss</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract"><code>extract</code></a></td>
<td>finds the concepts in a text</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Each task also has a reply cap: the most tokens that the model can write
in one reply. `TOKENS` gives the default of each task. A question has
options and a rubric, and an extract can name 15 concepts, so these two
get the most. A hint is short. The Settings page can change each cap.
Only the cap is a setting, because ramabana’s `oneshot` uses no other
per-call value: it turns thinking off, and the time limit of a model is
in ramabana’s `config.toml`. The model layer gives the cap to the API
models (OpenAI, Codex, Gemini, Copilot) and to the models on this Mac.
Claude Code does not use it for the reply, but ramabana uses it to fit
the prompt in the window of the model.

[`model_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#model_ask)
gives an `ask` for any model name. Install the `models` extra
(`pip install abhyasa[models]`) to use the full list of models. With the
extra, the name can be any model in that list: Claude Code, Codex,
OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, or a model on this machine (LiteRT, mlx,
llama.cpp, Ollama). The call goes through the routing of ramabana, as
[`route_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#route_ask)
below shows. Without the extra, the name goes to the model layer as it
is.

## Names for the model list

The Settings page shows a list of models. Each item has a name that
people know, such as “Claude Sonnet” or “GPT-5.5”. The model id, such as
`claude/sonnet`, is the value that the settings keep.
[`model_label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#model_label)
makes the name from the id. `PROVIDERS` gives the name of each group in
the list, and
[`provider_label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#provider_label)
reads it. ramabana’s `is_local` tells if a model runs on this Mac. For
Ollama, it looks at the daemon host (the `host` in config.toml, else
`$OLLAMA_HOST`), and it does not connect to it. Thus a model on an
Ollama daemon on another computer has no “a local model” name, and its
group is “Ollama on another computer”. Without the `models` extra, no
local model is in the list, so no name says “a local model”.

### model_label


*A name that people know for the model id `value`; `repo` is the
download of a local model, if known.*

Each kind of id gets a plain name. A Claude Code tier gets the word
Claude. A local model says so.

``` python
test_eq(model_label('claude/sonnet'), 'Claude Sonnet')
test_eq(model_label('claude/claude-opus-5-5'), 'Claude Opus 5.5')
test_eq(model_label('anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'), 'Claude Haiku 4.5')
test_eq(model_label('codex/gpt-6-astra'), 'GPT-6 Astra')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-5.4-mini'), 'GPT-5.4 Mini')
test_eq(model_label('gemini/gemini-3.5-flash'), 'Gemini 3.5 Flash')
test_eq(model_label('qwen-4b', 'mlx', 'mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit'), 'a local model: Qwen 3.5 4B')
test_eq(model_label('gemma-e4b', 'litert', 'litert-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-litert-lm'), 'a local model: Gemma 4 E4B')
test_eq(model_label('my-model', 'azure'), 'my-model')
```

An OpenAI id gets the name that OpenAI uses. A snapshot date such as
`2024-07-18` goes, so the name is the same as the name of the model.

``` python
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18'), 'GPT-4o mini')
test_eq(model_label('copilot/gpt-4-o-preview'), 'GPT-4o preview')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4o'), 'GPT-4o')
test_eq(model_label('openai/gpt-4.1-mini'), 'GPT-4.1 Mini')
```

The o-series names stay in lower case, with their hyphen:

``` python
test_eq(model_label('codex/o4-mini'), 'o4-mini')
test_eq(model_label('openai/o3'), 'o3')
```

One letter and a number stay together, as the maker writes them:

``` python
test_eq(model_label('copilot/kimi-k3'), 'Kimi K3')
test_eq(model_label('openrouter/qwen3-8b'), 'Qwen 3 8B')   # a longer word and a number still get a space
```

An Ollama model is local only when its daemon is on this Mac. With
`$OLLAMA_HOST` on localhost, the model and its group are on this Mac:

``` python
from fastcore.xtras import modified_env
```

``` python
with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='localhost:11434'):
    test_eq(model_label('ollama/qwen3:8b'), 'a local model: Qwen 3 8B')
    test_eq(provider_label('ollama', ['ollama/qwen3:8b']), 'On this Mac (Ollama)')
```

With `$OLLAMA_HOST` on another computer, the model is not called local,
and its group has a hosted name. The check reads only the host name: it
does not connect:

``` python
with modified_env(OLLAMA_HOST='http://gpu-box.lan:11434'):
    test_eq(model_label('ollama/qwen3:8b'), 'Qwen 3 8B')
    test_eq(provider_label('ollama', ['ollama/qwen3:8b']), 'Ollama on another computer')
```

The other groups keep their names from `PROVIDERS`. A provider that is
not in it gets its own name:

``` python
test_eq(provider_label('mlx', ['qwen-4b']), 'On this Mac (MLX)')
test_eq(provider_label('claude', ['claude/sonnet']), 'Claude')
test_eq(provider_label('groq'), 'Groq')
test_eq(provider_label(''), 'Other')
```

### Where a model runs

[`where_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#where_of)
says where the model `name` runs: `on this Mac` or `hosted`, and the
company of a hosted model. It uses

[`provider_label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#provider_label)
does, so an Ollama daemon on another computer is hosted. An unknown
model is hosted, as the guard takes it.
[`where_chip`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#where_chip)
gives the short text for the page.

### One row for each model

Some models come through two providers. For example, Claude Haiku 5.5
comes through Claude Code and through GitHub Copilot, and GPT-6.1 Sol
through Codex, GitHub Copilot and the OpenAI API. Each route has its own
id, so the list showed the same name two or three times.
[`one_each`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#one_each)
keeps one row for each name: the route of the first provider in
ramabana’s `READY_ORDER` (subscriptions first, then keys). The row keeps
the other ids in `also`. A saved id (`keep`) always stays, so the list
shows the choice that you made.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/llm.py#L186"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### one_each

``` python
def one_each(
    rows:list, keep:str=''
)->list:
```

*One row of
[`rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/settings.html#rows) for
each model name, in the first place of that name: the saved id `keep`,
else the route that ramabana tries first. `also` has the other ids. An
alias with a version beside it goes into the `also` of the newest
version.*

Claude Haiku 5.5 shows one time, on Claude Code. With the Copilot id
saved, the Copilot row stays.

``` python
dup = [dict(value='copilot/claude-haiku-5.5', name='Claude Haiku 5.5', provider='copilot'), dict(value='claude/sonnet', name='Claude Sonnet', provider='claude'),
       dict(value='claude/claude-haiku-5-5', name='Claude Haiku 5.5', provider='claude')]
test_eq([(r['value'], r['also']) for r in one_each(dup)], [('claude/claude-haiku-5-5', ['copilot/claude-haiku-5.5']), ('claude/sonnet', [])])
test_eq(one_each(dup, keep='copilot/claude-haiku-5.5')[0]['value'], 'copilot/claude-haiku-5.5')
```

An alias such as `claude/opus` and its version, such as Claude Opus 5.5,
are one model. The list shows only the version, with the alias in
`also`. A saved alias stays.

``` python
al = [dict(value='claude/opus', name='Claude Opus', provider='claude'), dict(value='claude/claude-opus-4-1', name='Claude Opus 4.1', provider='claude'),
      dict(value='claude/claude-opus-5-5', name='Claude Opus 5.5', provider='claude'), dict(value='codex/gpt-5', name='GPT-5', provider='codex'),
      dict(value='codex/gpt-5-mini', name='GPT-5 Mini', provider='codex')]
test_eq([(r['name'], r['also']) for r in one_each(al)], [('Claude Opus 4.1', []), ('Claude Opus 5.5', ['claude/opus']), ('GPT-5', []), ('GPT-5 Mini', [])])
test_eq([r['name'] for r in one_each(al, keep='claude/opus')][:2], ['Claude Opus', 'Claude Opus 4.1'])
```

[`Router`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#router) is the
`ask` the app gives the tutor. Called as it is, it uses the default
model. `for_(task)` gives the `ask` for one task: the model the settings
name for it, else the default. `for_(task, name, job)` gives the `ask`
for `task` on the model `name`, on the ramabana job `job`. The Test
button of the Settings page uses the job `test:<task>`, so a test does
not move the job of the task. When the default routes by task, as
[`RouteAsk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#routeask)
below does, `for_` lets it make the `ask`. `cap(task)` gives the reply
cap of the task, read on each call. `warm` starts the backend of each
task in the background.

``` python
dflt = Fake(dflt='default')
r = Router(dflt, models=lambda: {})
test_eq(r('x'), 'default')
test_is(r.for_('grade'), dflt)
named = Fake(dflt='named'); named.model = 'fast'
_asks['fast'] = named
r = Router(dflt, models=lambda: dict(grade='fast'))
test_eq(r.for_('grade')('x'), 'named')
test_eq(r.for_('question')('x'), 'default')
test_is(for_task(dflt, 'grade'), dflt)
```

## Every call through ramabana

ramabana is the agent layer on top of the model layer. Its `Routing`
sends each job to a model. When a cloud model fails or gives no answer,
`Routing` puts it aside for five minutes and sends the job to the next
route: other cloud models, then a small model on this Mac. Its backends
stay open, so a call does not pay the start time of a new `Chat`.

[`ramabana_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_agent)
makes one ramabana `Agent` for the process, on the first call. The
`Agent` gets only what `Agent.oneshot` needs:

- `NullHost`: no folders, and each file operation is refused.
- `readonly=True`, no sub-agents, no extensions, no skills, no lessons:
  no tool can write, run code or go on the network.
- Approvals that refuse when nobody answers, and no saved rules.
- `cfg=None`: no history, plan or run log, so the `Agent` writes no
  files.
- A short briefing, so that it does not read skills or project files.

The turn of the `Agent` is the default model, so a task whose model
fails goes to the default model first.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/llm.py#L253"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ramabana_agent

``` python
def ramabana_agent(
    turn:str=None
):
```

*The one ramabana `Agent` of this process, made on first use on the turn
`dflt_model(turn)`: no folders, no tool that acts, no files.*

Each task is a ramabana job with the same name.
[`_point`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#_point) sets
the model of the job before each call, only when the settings changed
it. A model that ramabana put aside stays aside until its time is up.

[`ramabana_oneshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_oneshot)
asks one question on the job of a task. ramabana’s `Backend.oneshot`
does not wait when another call holds the backend: it gives ’’. So the
call holds the abhyasa lock of each backend that it uses.
`Agent.oneshot` calls `fits(b)` just before it asks the backend `b`, on
the first route and on each fallback. `fits` lets go of the lock of the
route before, then waits for the lock of `b`. A call holds one lock at a
time, so two calls cannot wait for each other. When no route gives an
answer, the call raises.

A failure can take some time: ramabana tries each route in turn, then
the small model on this Mac. It puts a failed cloud model aside for five
minutes.

A route can also raise ramabana’s `OneshotTimeout` when a call goes past
its deadline.
[`timeout_error`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#timeout_error)
changes it into the same `RuntimeError` as a call with no answer. The
error names the model and the seconds, so each caller catches one kind
of error.

`prepare` lets the caller change the text for each route, as ramabana’s
`Agent.oneshot` does. The guide uses it for its guard: the guard then
knows if the model of the route is on this Mac. `HOSTED` is the model
that a guard takes when it does not know the route.

``` python
def ramabana_oneshot(
    job:str, name:str, prompt:str, sp:str='', max_tokens:int=4096, prepare:NoneType=None
)->str:
```

*Ask
[`prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/prompts.html#prompt) on
the ramabana job `job`, pointed at the model `name`. Wait for a busy
backend. Raise when no route answers. `prepare(prompt, sp, backend)`
gives the text for each route, so a guard knows the model that gets it.*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### timeout_error

``` python
def timeout_error(
    job:str, e, name:str=''
)->RuntimeError:
```

*The `RuntimeError` for the ramabana `OneshotTimeout` `e` on the job
`job`: it names the model (`name`, else the route of `e`) and the
seconds.*

[`ramabana_stream`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_stream)
is the twin of
[`ramabana_oneshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_oneshot)
that gives the reply as the model sends it, through ramabana’s
`Agent.oneshot_stream`. It holds the same lock of each backend, and it
raises the same errors. The guard (`prepare`) runs before the stream
starts. A route that cannot stream (ramabana’s `StreamUnsupported`,
before it sends anything) gives the whole reply of
[`ramabana_oneshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_oneshot)
as one chunk, so the caller does not need a second path.

``` python
def ramabana_stream(
    job:str, name:str, prompt:str, sp:str='', max_tokens:int=4096, prepare:NoneType=None

```

*The reply of
[`ramabana_oneshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_oneshot),
one chunk at a time as the model sends it. A route that cannot stream
gives the whole reply as one chunk. Raise when no route answers.*

[`RouteAsk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#routeask) is
the default `ask` of the web app. `via(task, name, max_tokens)` gives
the `ask` of one task, and
[`Router.for_`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#router.for_)
uses it. A call with no task goes to the job `ask:<model>`. `warm`
starts the backend of each task, with no model call.
[`route_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#route_ask)
gives a
[`RouteAsk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#routeask)
when ramabana is installed, else
[`rishi_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#rishi_ask)
with a warning.

### The worker agent

[`ramabana_worker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_worker)
makes a second ramabana `Agent`, for the gather agent of research. It is
never the one `Agent` of
[`ramabana_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_agent),
so a long gather never holds a one-shot call. It runs on the default
routing (`Routing(turn=dflt_model())`). Its host is the shalya `host`
(default: a `NullHost`, with no folders). The caller names its tools in
`tools`, then adds them with `add_tool`. ramabana’s `only_tools` offers
the model only those tools, and refuses a tool with another name.
ramabana’s memory and plan tools are held back. It has no approvals
listener, so a tool that writes is refused. The caps stop a turn after
`max_calls` tool calls, `max_steps` model steps, `max_tokens` tokens or
`max_cost` dollars. A model such as Claude Code on a plan reports no
cost. Then ramabana estimates the dollars from the tokens at the price
of the model
([`ramabana.agent.token_rate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#token_rate)),
and keeps the estimate in `estimated`, so the dollar cap still holds.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/llm.py#L386"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ramabana_lead

``` python
def ramabana_lead(
    read_roots:tuple=(), tools:list=(), sp:str='You are the source gatherer of abhyasa, a tutor.', turn:str=None,
    minutes:float=15, max_calls:int=300, max_steps:int=80, max_cost:float=5.0, max_tokens:int=2000000
)->tuple:
```

*`(agent, host)`: a new ramabana `Agent` made by ramabana’s `mk_agent`,
with its own read and web tools (`LEAD_TOOLS`) and its* sub-agents
(`delegate_search`, at most 4 at once in the whole tree), on the turn
`dflt_model(turn)`. Its sub-agents run on ramabana’s `subagent` route.
The folders `read_roots` are open for reads only; its one folder that it
may write is a new empty one. It has no Python (`python='off'`), no
vault, and no approvals listener, so each tool that writes is refused.
The model sees only `LEAD_TOOLS` and the tools named in `tools`, when
the caller adds them. The caps: `max_calls` tool calls in the whole
tree, `max_steps` model steps, `max_tokens` tokens and `max_cost`
dollars for a turn, and
[`minutes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#minutes)
for a sub-agent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/llm.py#L372"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ramabana_worker

``` python
def ramabana_worker(
    tools:list=(), host:NoneType=None, sp:str='You are the source gatherer of abhyasa, a tutor.', turn:str=None,
    max_calls:int=300, max_steps:int=80, max_cost:float=5.0, max_tokens:int=2000000
):
```

*A new ramabana `Agent` on the turn `dflt_model(turn)`, with the shalya
`host` (default: no folders). The model sees only the tools named in
`tools`, when the caller adds them. Never the agent of
[`ramabana_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ramabana_agent).
A turn stops at `max_tokens` tokens, and at `max_cost` dollars
(estimated from the tokens when the model reports no cost).*

The worker offers only the tool that the test names and adds. It is a
new `Agent` each time, and never the shared one. The caps reach the
`Agent`.

``` python
if _has_ramabana():
    def look(q:str, # what to look for
             ) -> str:
        "Look for `q`."
        return q
    w = ramabana_worker(['look'], max_calls=50, max_tokens=1000)
    w.add_tool(look)
    test_eq([t.__name__ for t in w.tools], ['look'])
    assert w is not ramabana_worker() and w is not ramabana_agent()
    test_eq((w.readonly, w.subagents, w.tool_budget, w.max_cost, w.max_tokens), (True, False, 50, WORKER_DOLLARS, 1000))
```

The worker refuses a tool that `tools` does not name. A worker with no
names offers no tool, so ramabana’s own tools stay out.

``` python
if _has_ramabana():
    def write(path:str, # the file
              ) -> str:
        "Write `path`."
        return path
    test_fail(lambda: w.add_tool(write), contains='not in only_tools')
    test_eq(ramabana_worker().tools, [])
```

When the model reports no cost, ramabana estimates the dollars from the
tokens with its own price table (`est_rate` is None), and keeps them in
`estimated`. A new worker has estimated nothing, and has the default
token cap.

``` python
if _has_ramabana():
    w = ramabana_worker()
    test_eq((w.est_rate, w.estimated, w.max_tokens), (None, 0., WORKER_TOKENS))
```

The lead of research is made by ramabana’s `mk_agent`. It offers
ramabana’s read and web tools and `delegate_search`, and the tool that
the test adds. It has no tool that writes a file or runs a command. The
folder of the learner is open for reads only.

``` python
if _has_ramabana():
    import tempfile, shutil
```

``` python
if _has_ramabana():
    ro = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    a, h = ramabana_lead([ro], ['look'], minutes=2)
    a.add_tool(look)
    names = {t.__name__ for t in a.tools}
    assert {'view_file', 'read_url', 'web_search', 'delegate_search', 'look'} <= names, names
    assert not names & {'run_shell', 'run_python', 'create_file', 'replace_text', 'git_commit', 'add_root'}, names
    test_eq((h.read_roots, a.subagent_timeout, a.subagent_writes), ([str(Path(ro).resolve())], 120, False))
    a.close(); shutil.rmtree(h.scratch, ignore_errors=True)
```

### Tests of the route

These tests use a ramabana `Agent` with fake backends from
`ramabana.testing`, so no model runs. `using(a)` puts that `Agent` in
place of the real one for one test. CI does not install the `models`
extra, so these tests run only when ramabana is installed.

``` python
from contextlib import contextmanager
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
```

``` python
if has_rama:
    from ramabana.core import resolve
    from ramabana.testing import fake_agent, FakeBackend
```

``` python
@contextmanager
def using(a):
    "Use the `Agent` `a` in place of the real one, for one test."
    _ra['agent'] = a
    try: yield a
    finally: _ra.pop('agent', None)
```

Each task goes to the ramabana job with the same name. The task that the
settings name gets its model, the other tasks get the default. Each call
asks for the reply cap of its task, `TOKENS[task]`, so a long question
with its rubric is not cut.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku'), tokens=lambda: {})
        test_eq(r.for_('grade')('hi'), 'ONESHOT:hi')
        test_eq(r.for_('question').model, 'claude/sonnet')
        r.for_('question')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', TOKENS['grade']), ('question', TOKENS['question'])])
    test_eq((a.routing.policy['grade'], a.routing.policy['question']), ('claude/haiku', 'claude/sonnet'))
```

A change in the settings has an effect on the next call, with no
restart. An empty choice goes back to the default.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    ms = dict(grade='claude/haiku')
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: ms)
        r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/haiku')
        ms['grade'] = 'claude/opus'; r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/opus')
        ms['grade'] = ''; r.for_('grade')('hi'); test_eq(a.routing.policy['grade'], 'claude/sonnet')
```

`prepare` gets each route. Here it writes the name of the model before
the prompt, so the reply shows what the route got:

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    with using(a): test_eq(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('hint', prepare=lambda p, sp, b: (f'{b.spec.name} {p}', sp))('hi'), 'ONESHOT:fake hi')
```

`Slow` is a fake backend that takes a moment to answer. It sets `inside`
when a call starts.

``` python
if has_rama:
    class Slow(FakeBackend):
        "A fake backend that answers after 0.2 s and sets `inside` when a call starts."
        def __init__(self, *a, **kw): super().__init__(*a, **kw); self.inside = threading.Event()
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): self.inside.set(); time.sleep(0.2); return f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'
```

This is why the route has a lock. ramabana’s `Agent.oneshot` does not
wait for a busy backend: a second call at the same time gets ’’.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); slow = Slow(); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': slow
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        f1 = ex.submit(a.oneshot, 'one'); slow.inside.wait(); f2 = ex.submit(a.oneshot, 'two')
    test_eq((f1.result(), f2.result()), ('ONESHOT:one', ''))
```

Through the route, the second call waits for the first, and both calls
get an answer.

``` python
if has_rama:
    slow.inside.clear()
    with using(a), ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        ask = RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('question')
        f1 = ex.submit(ask, 'one'); slow.inside.wait(); f2 = ex.submit(ask, 'two')
        test_eq((f1.result(), f2.result()), ('ONESHOT:one', 'ONESHOT:two'))
```

When no route gives an answer, the call raises. The error names the
task, the model and the note of ramabana, so
[`ask_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#ask_json)
never gets ’’.

``` python
if has_rama:
    class Empty(FakeBackend):
        "A fake cloud backend that answers nothing."
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): return ''
    a, _ = fake_agent(); empty = Empty(resolve('claude/haiku')); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': empty
    with using(a):
        ask = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku')).for_('grade')
        test_fail(lambda: ask('hi'), contains='grade task')
        try: ask('hi')
        except RuntimeError as e: assert 'claude/haiku' in str(e) and 'answered nothing' in str(e), e
```

A route that goes past its deadline raises ramabana’s `OneshotTimeout`.
The call raises the same `RuntimeError`, with the model and the seconds,
and keeps the first error as its cause.

``` python
if has_rama:
    from ramabana.runtime import OneshotTimeout
```

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent()
    def late(*a, **kw): raise OneshotTimeout('claude/haiku', 31.6, True)
    a.oneshot = late
    with using(a):
        try: RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade')('hi'); assert False, 'no error'
        except RuntimeError as e:
            test_eq(str(e), 'The grade task got no answer from claude/haiku through ramabana: claude/haiku did not answer in 32 seconds.')
            assert isinstance(e.__cause__, OneshotTimeout)
```

### Tests of the stream

`Chunks` is a fake backend that can stream: it sends its reply three
letters at a time. `ask.stream` gives the chunks in order, and their
join is the reply. The guard of `prepare` sees the route before the
stream starts.

``` python
if has_rama:
    class Chunks(FakeBackend):
        "A fake backend that streams `ONESHOT:<prompt>` in chunks of 3 letters."
        supports_stream = True
        def _oneshot_stream(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): return (f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(f'ONESHOT:{prompt}'), 3))
    a, _ = fake_agent(); ch = Chunks(resolve('claude/haiku')); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': ch
    with using(a): got = list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint', prepare=lambda p, sp, b: (f'{b.spec.name} {p}', sp)).stream('hi'))
    test_eq(''.join(got), 'ONESHOT:claude/haiku hi')
    assert len(got) > 1
```

A backend that cannot stream (the default of `FakeBackend`) gives the
whole reply of the blocking call as one chunk:

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    with using(a): test_eq(list(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet').via('hint').stream('hi')), ['ONESHOT:hi'])
```

The stream lets go of the lock of its backend at the end, so the next
call on that backend does not wait:

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': ch
    with using(a):
        list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint').stream('one'))
        assert _lock(ch).acquire(timeout=1); _lock(ch).release()
        it = RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('hint').stream('two'); next(it); it.close()   # a stream that stops early lets go too
        assert _lock(ch).acquire(timeout=1); _lock(ch).release()
```

A stream with no text raises the same error as a blocking call, and a
timeout raises the same `RuntimeError`:

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, _ = fake_agent(); empty = Empty(resolve('claude/haiku')); empty.supports_stream = True
    empty._oneshot_stream = lambda prompt, sp, max_tokens: (c for c in ())
    a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': empty
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade').stream('hi')), contains='grade task')
    def late(*a, **kw): raise OneshotTimeout('claude/haiku', 31.6, True); yield
    a.oneshot_stream = late
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: list(RouteAsk('claude/haiku').via('grade').stream('hi')), contains='did not answer in 32 seconds')
```

The next tests need ramabana’s real `Routing`, so that a failed model
goes to its next route. `routed_agent` gives a fake `Agent` with the
real `Routing` on two fake models: `fake-main`, the default, and
`fake-quick`. They are hosted models with a fake key, so `Routing` takes
them on any machine. `make(spec)` gives the fake backend of each model,
and `bes` keeps them by name.

``` python
if has_rama:
    from ramabana.core import register_model, Routing
```

``` python
if has_rama:
    os.environ['ABHYASA_FAKE_KEY'] = 'not a real key'
    for n in ('fake-main', 'fake-quick'): register_model(n, f'fakevendor/{n}', runtime='remote', api_key_env='ABHYASA_FAKE_KEY')

    def routed_agent(make):
        "A fake `Agent` on the real `Routing`, with the turn on `fake-main`. Returns the `Agent` and the backends by model name."
        a, _ = fake_agent(routing=Routing(turn='fake-main'))
        del a._be_or_none   # the real one, which asks `Routing`
        bes = {}
        def be(job='turn'):
            s = a.routing.spec(job)
            if s.name not in bes: bes[s.name] = make(s)
            return bes[s.name]
        a._be = be
        return a, bes
```

A fallback holds the lock of the backend that it goes to. Here
`fake-quick` answers nothing, so the `grade` call goes to `fake-main`. A
`question` call on `fake-main` starts while that fallback runs. It waits
for the lock, and both calls get an answer.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, bes = routed_agent(lambda s: Slow(s) if s.name != 'fake-quick' else Empty(s))
    with using(a), ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        g = ex.submit(Router(RouteAsk('fake-main'), models=lambda: dict(grade='fake-quick'), tokens=lambda: {}).for_('grade'), 'g')
        while 'fake-main' not in bes: time.sleep(0.01)
        bes['fake-main'].inside.wait()
        q = ex.submit(RouteAsk('fake-main').via('question'), 'q')
        test_eq((g.result(), q.result()), ('ONESHOT:g', 'ONESHOT:q'))
```

When no route answers, each route is tried one time. The last route is
the small model on this Mac, `gemma-e4b`.

``` python
if has_rama:
    calls = Counter()
    class Counted(Empty):
        "A fake backend that answers nothing and counts its calls."
        def _oneshot(self, prompt, sp, max_tokens): calls[self.spec.name] += 1; return ''
    a, bes = routed_agent(Counted)
    with using(a): test_fail(lambda: RouteAsk('fake-main').via('grade', 'fake-quick')('hi'), contains='grade task')
    test_eq(calls['gemma-e4b'], 1)
    test_eq(set(calls.values()), {1})
```

`warm` asks ramabana for the backend of each task in the background, and
sends nothing to the model. It gives the thread. The jobs of `WARM`
start too: the `guide` job, on the model of the screen guide (the model
for hints when it has none). `warm(['guide'])` starts only the guide.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent(); seen = []
    a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': seen.append(job) or be
    with using(a):
        Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: {}).warm().join()
    test_eq(seen, [*TASKS, 'guide'])
    test_eq(be.sent, [])
    seen.clear()
    with using(a): Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku')).warm(['guide']).join()
    test_eq((seen, a.routing.policy['guide']), (['guide'], 'claude/haiku'))
    with using(a): Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(hint='claude/haiku', guide='claude/opus')).warm(['guide']).join()
    test_eq(a.routing.policy['guide'], 'claude/opus')   # a model of its own wins
```

With ramabana,
[`route_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#route_ask)
gives a
[`RouteAsk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#routeask).
Without it,
[`route_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#route_ask)
gives
[`rishi_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#rishi_ask)
and a warning that says so one time.

``` python
import sys, warnings
from unittest.mock import patch
```

``` python
if has_rama: assert isinstance(route_ask(), RouteAsk)
with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'ramabana': None}), warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    ask = route_ask('claude/haiku')
test_eq(ask.model, 'claude/haiku')
assert not isinstance(ask, RouteAsk) and 'ramabana' in str(w[0].message)
```

### The reply cap of each task

A reply cap comes from the settings table (`tokens.<task>`), from 1 to
`TOKENS_MAX`. A cap that you typed in the file as text, such as `"900"`,
works too.

``` python
from abhyasa.settings import update_settings, val
```

``` python
update_settings('tokens', hint=' 900 ')
test_eq(val('tokens.hint'), 900)
update_settings('tokens', hint=str(TOKENS_MAX + 1))
test_eq(val('tokens.hint'), TOKENS_MAX)   # clamped to the top
update_settings('tokens', hint=None)
```

[`Router.cap`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/llm.html#router.cap)
gives the saved cap of a task, else the default of the task. A bad value
in the settings file gives the default, so a call never fails because of
it.

``` python
caps = dict(hint=300)
r = Router(Fake(), models=lambda: {}, tokens=lambda: caps)
test_eq(r.cap('hint'), 300)
test_eq(r.cap('grade'), TOKENS['grade'])
caps['hint'] = 'lots'; test_eq(r.cap('hint'), TOKENS['hint'])
caps['hint'] = 99999; test_eq(r.cap('hint'), TOKENS_MAX)          # out of range: the most
```

A task after
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
([`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/journey.html#plan),
[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/model.html#pick), `note`,
`profile`) borrows the model, the reply cap and the job of an older task
until it has a model of its own.

``` python
class Via:
    model = 'base'
    def __call__(self, p, sp=''): return ''
    def via(self, job, name='', cap=None): return (job, name, cap)
ms = dict(extract='x/extract', hint='x/hint')
r = Router(Via(), models=lambda: ms, tokens=lambda: {})
test_eq((r.for_('plan'), r.for_('note')), (('extract', 'x/extract', 4096), ('hint', 'x/hint', 512)))
ms['plan'] = 'x/plan'
test_eq(r.for_('plan'), ('plan', 'x/plan', 4096))
```

The cap reaches `Agent.oneshot`, and a change has an effect on the next
call.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    caps = dict(grade=777)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: {}, tokens=lambda: caps)
        r.for_('grade')('hi'); caps['grade'] = ''; r.for_('grade')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', 777), ('grade', TOKENS['grade'])])
```

The Test button of the Settings page asks on its own job, `test:<task>`,
with the cap of the task. The job of the task stays where the settings
put it.

``` python
if has_rama:
    a, be = fake_agent()
    jobs, one = [], a.oneshot
    a.oneshot = lambda p, sp='', job='oneshot', max_tokens=None, fits=None: jobs.append((job, max_tokens)) or one(p, sp, job, max_tokens, fits)
    with using(a):
        r = Router(RouteAsk('claude/sonnet'), models=lambda: dict(grade='claude/haiku'), tokens=lambda: {})
        r.for_('grade')('hi')
        r.for_('grade', 'claude/opus', job='test:grade')('hi')
    test_eq(jobs, [('grade', TOKENS['grade']), ('test:grade', TOKENS['grade'])])
    test_eq((a.routing.policy['grade'], a.routing.policy['test:grade']), ('claude/haiku', 'claude/opus'))
```
